spots.name: Basilica of St. Sernin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Saint-Sernin is a church in Toulouse, France, the former abbey church of the Abbey of Saint-Sernin or St Saturnin. Apart from the church, none of the abbey buildings remain.

spots.name: Canal du Midi
spots.summary: The Canal du Midi is a 240 km (150 mi) long canal in Southern France. Originally named the Canal Royal en Languedoc and renamed by French revolutionaries to Canal du Midi in 1789, the canal is considered one of the greatest construction works of the 17th century.

spots.name: Muséum de Toulouse

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Muséum de Toulouse is a museum of natural history in Toulouse, France. It is located in the Busca-Montplaisir neighborhood of the city, houses a collection of more than 2.5 million items, and has some 3,000 square metres (32,000 sq ft) of exhibition space. Its Index Herbariorum code is TLM.

spots.name: Capitole de Toulouse
spots.summary: The Capitole de Toulouse, commonly known as the Capitole, is the heart of the municipal administration and the city hall of the French city of Toulouse. It was designated a monument historique by the French government in 1840.

names.ja: キャピトール・ド・トゥールーズ

spots.name: Toulouse Cathedral
spots.summary: Toulouse Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church located in the city of Toulouse, France. The cathedral is a national monument, and is the seat of the Archbishop of Toulouse. It has been listed since 1862 as a monument historique by the French Ministry of Culture.

spots.name: Musée Saint-Raymond

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Musée Saint-Raymond is the archeological museum of Toulouse, France, opened in 1892. The site originally was a necropolis, and in later constructions was a hospital for the poor and pilgrims, prison, student residence, stables, barracks and presbytery, eventually becoming a museum in 1891.

names.fr: Musée Saint-Raymond, musée d'Archéologie de Toulouse
names.ja: サン・レイモン博物館

spots.name: Church of the Jacobins
spots.summary: The Church of the Jacobins is a deconsecrated Roman Catholic church located in Toulouse, France. It is a large brick building whose construction started in 1230, and whose architecture influenced the development of the Gothique méridional style. The relics of Thomas Aquinas are housed there.

names.es: Convento de los Dominicos de Toulouse

spots.name: Musée des Augustins

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed

spots.summary: The Musée des Augustins de Toulouse is a fine arts museum in Toulouse, France which conserves a collection of sculpture and paintings from the Middle Ages to the early 20th century.

names.ja: オーギュスタン美術館

spots.name: Cité de l'espace

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Cité de l'espace is a scientific discovery centre in France focused on spaceflight. It was opened in June 1997, and is located on the eastern outskirts of Toulouse.

spots.name: Toulouse-Matabiau station
spots.summary: Toulouse-Matabiau is the main railway station in Toulouse, southern France. It is in the city centre and connected to the Toulouse Metro. The station is situated on the Bordeaux–Sète railway, Toulouse–Bayonne railway, Brive–Toulouse railway and Toulouse–Auch railway. Direct trains run to most parts of France.

names.ja: トゥールーズ・マタビオ駅

spots.name: Pont-Neuf
spots.summary: The Pont Neuf, French for "New Bridge", is a bridge from the 16th and 17th centuries in Toulouse, in the South of France.

spots.name: Notre-Dame de la Daurade
spots.summary: Notre-Dame de la Daurade is a basilica in Toulouse, France. It was established in 410 when Emperor Honorius allowed the conversion of pagan temples to Christianity. The original building of Notre-Dame de la Daurade was a temple dedicated to Apollo.

names.fr: Basilique de la Daurade de Toulouse
names.es: Basílica de la Dorada de Toulouse
names.it: Basilica di Notre-Dame de la Daurade

spots.name: Notre-Dame du Taur

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Notre-Dame du Taur is a Roman Catholic church located in Toulouse, France. According to legend, the edifice was built on the exact spot where the body of Saint Saturnin (Sernin), patron saint of Toulouse, became detached from the bull that dragged the martyr to his death.

names.es: Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Taur

spots.name: Jardin des Plantes, Toulouse
spots.summary: The Jardin des Plantes is a public park and botanical garden located on Allée Jules-Guesde, Toulouse, France.

spots.name: Théâtre du Capitole
spots.summary: The Théâtre du Capitole de Toulouse is an opera house within the main administration buildings, the Capitole, of the city of Toulouse in south-west France. It houses an opera company, ballet company and symphony orchestra, Orchestre national du Capitole de Toulouse.

names.ja: テアトル・ドゥ・カピトル

spots.name: Hôtel d'Assézat
spots.summary: The Hôtel d'Assézat in Toulouse, France, is a French Renaissance hôtel particulier of the 16th century which houses the Bemberg Foundation, a major art gallery of the city.

names.ja: バンベルグ財団美術館

spots.name: Jardin botanique Henri Gaussen
spots.summary: The Jardin botanique Henri Gaussen is a botanical garden operated by the Université Paul Sabatier at 39 allées Jules Guesde, Toulouse, Haute-Garonne, Midi-Pyrénées, France. It is open weekdays in the warmer months.

spots.name: Hôtel-Dieu Saint-Jacques

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Hôtel-Dieu Saint-Jacques is a former hospital in Toulouse, located at 2 rue Charles-Viguerie. Already in operation in the 12th century on the left bank of the Garonne River, it became the largest hospital in Toulouse following numerous expansions in the 17th and 18th centuries.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.name: rue d'Alsace-Lorraine
spots.summary: Rue d'Alsace-Lorraine is a road in Toulouse, capital of the Occitania, in the South of France.

spots.name: Augustinian convent

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed

spots.summary: The Augustinian Convent of Toulouse was founded in 1286 for members of the Augustinian religious order. It was first established outside the city walls, near the Matabiau quarter, then, between 1310 and 1341 moved to the corner of rue du Musée and rue des Arts. In 1790 it ceased to be a convent.

spots.name: Château d'eau

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Château d'Eau is a nineteenth century water tower, near the cours Dillon, beside the Pont-Neuf, in Toulouse, France. The building and its pumping station have been listed as historical monuments since 28 September 1987.

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: Les Abattoirs, Musée – Frac Occitanie Toulouse, combines a museum of modern and contemporary art (Musée) and a regional collection of contemporary art (Frac). It is located in the French Occitanie region, in the city of Toulouse. Les Abattoirs keep approximately 3,880 works and objects of all origins.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The church of the Sanctuaire Saint-Jérôme, rue du Lieutenant-Colonel-Pélissier, is a church built by the Compagnie royale des Pénitents bleus de Toulouse. It was built in the 17th century by architect Pierre Levesville under Louis XIII, the first French king to join the brotherhood.

spots.name: Saint Nicolas Church, Toulouse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint-Nicolas Church is located in Saint Cyprien neighbourhood on the west side of the Garonne River, just outside the old city walls of Toulouse. Nicknamed "The Beautiful Unknown/Stranger", it is the second oldest church of the city.

spots.name: Maison Seilhan

hours.note: Closed Mon, Thu, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: The Maison Seilhan, is a historic residence in Toulouse, France, considered the place where the Order of Preachers was founded. It was given to Dominic de Guzmán during the division of the inheritance of Bernard Seilhan, a local magistrate of the Count of Toulouse, on 25 April 1215.

spots.name: Hôtel de Bagis
spots.summary: The Hôtel de Bagis in Toulouse, France, is a Renaissance hôtel particulier (palace) of the 16th century. It is a listed historical monument since 1889.

spots.name: Saint-Michel prison
spots.summary: Saint-Michel prison is a former penal institution located in Toulouse, in service from 1872 to 2009, known for its role during the Occupation and its characteristic 19th century architecture.

spots.name: Stadium de Toulouse
spots.summary: Stadium de Toulouse, previously named Stadium Municipal, is the largest multi-purpose stadium in Toulouse, France. It is currently used mostly for football matches, mainly those of the Toulouse Football Club, as well as rugby matches for Stade Toulousain in the European Rugby Champions Cup and Top 14.

spots.summary: The Hôtel de Bernuy in rue Léon Gambetta, Toulouse, France, is a Renaissance hôtel particulier (palace) of the 16th century built by the mason Louis Privat for the wealthy woad merchant, Jean de Bernuy.

spots.summary: A team and a welcome at the top. Local products cooked with passion. The service is very warm and attentive. More than reasonable in view of the quality of the products. Original dishes, elaborate, homemade, a lot of work behind. Very welcoming staff and a beautiful ambiance.

spots.summary: Friendly place, friendly team. Always a pleasure to come and eat in this warm little place, the meal is always delicious, exceptional prawn risotto. For lovers of duck breast it is tasty and melts in the mouth. Large terrace.

spots.summary: This Turkish place is quite popular with students, and it's not hard to see why when they serve a generous portion of good food at low prices.
